title: Circular Measure Module 5 Lesson 1: Annular Sectors & Concentric Rings custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values, configurations and requested combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs reasoning scope only.

parts.prompt: An annular sector is bounded between concentric circles of radii $3\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$, and subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$. Find its exact area in terms of $\pi$.

An annular sector has inner radius $4\text{ cm}$, outer radius $7\text{ cm}$, and subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact sum of the lengths of its two curved circular arc boundaries.

An annular sector has inner radius $2\text{ cm}$, outer radius $6\text{ cm}$, and central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$. Find its exact total perimeter, including its two straight radial edges.
An annular sector bounded between concentric circles of radii $2\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$ has an area of $8\pi\text{ cm}^2$. Find its central angle $\theta$ in radians.
An annular sector with inner radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$ has an area of $\dfrac{11\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^2$. Find its exact outer radius $R$.
In an annular sector, the outer radius is $3$ times the inner radius ($R = 3r$). Find the exact ratio of the area of the annular sector to the area of the inner un-removed sector.
An annular sector has inner radius $3$ cm, radial width $2$ cm and angle $\pi/3$. Find its area and complete perimeter exactly.
